gaps.sentence: The doctor has ___ detailed records of every patient since 1990.
gaps.explanation: keep records (of something) is the fixed collocation for storing information.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: We should ___ an effort to arrive on time.
gaps.explanation: make an effort is the fixed collocation meaning to try hard.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.

gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: He was exhausted because he had ___ the cooking for twenty people.
gaps.explanation: do the cooking is the fixed phrase; after 'had' the past participle 'done' is needed.

gaps.sentence: We ___ a visit to the museum while we were in Vienna.
gaps.explanation: pay a visit to somebody/something means to go and see them briefly.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our shopping at the local market every Saturday.
gaps.explanation: do the shopping is the collocation for buying food and household goods.
